notes: fold(k) = k with ASCII A-Z mapped to a-z and every other byte unchanged. Nothing else folds.

keyCheck(k): 'refuse_charset' unless k is non-empty and every character is in %x20-7E; else 'refuse_reserved' if fold(k) equals fold(r) for any r in 'reserved'; else 'accept'. Charset is checked FIRST.

payloadCheck(json): applied to the TOP-LEVEL keys of the decoded JWT payload, each key taken AFTER JSON string unescaping. 'refuse' if any key fails the charset, if two keys (duplicates included) have equal fold, or if a key that is not byte-equal to a reserved name has a fold equal to one. Otherwise 'accept'. Nested objects are not inspected.

payload_json is the payload as raw JSON TEXT (a JSON string here) because duplicate keys cannot be represented in a parsed object. Runners MUST read the keys from the raw text with a duplicate-preserving tokenizer, never by decoding into a map first.

reserved is issuer/internal/tokens/tokens.go reservedClaims PLUS 'acr' (owner ruling 8, 2026-11-14: acr is reserved from issuer v0.151.0; the issuer list read on 2026-11-14 did not yet hold it, so the issuer's drift test against this file goes red until I4 adds it). A runner MUST assert its own language's reserved set equals this list.

keys.why: '-' does not fold to '_'; a migrating product's real key
SPACE is printable ASCII and no decoder binds ' sub' to sub
ASCII fold equals a reserved name
U+017F LONG S: Unicode simple fold maps it to 's'; refused by charset before any fold
U+0130: Java toLowerCase gives 'i', Go EqualFold does not; the charset rule makes the difference unreachable
owner ruling 8: the SDKs read acr as an MFA marker, so a partner must not mint it
U+017F + 'id' (folds to 'sid' under Unicode simple folding); named in issuer ADR-097 AF-097.2's minimum list

payloads.why: fold collision with a reserved name
escaped U+017F; after unescaping the key is non-ASCII (e-02 run-issuer.log)
reserved name absent, fold variant present: encoding/json would bind it
an escaped ASCII 'S': the check runs on the UNESCAPED key
exact duplicate: decoders disagree on which wins
KELVIN SIGN sorts last and would override a present claim in encoding/json
nested keys are not claims; only top-level keys are checked
' sub' is not a fold of 'sub'
non-ASCII key: no issuer from this release mints one
upper-case variant alongside the real claim
fold variant of the now-reserved acr (owner ruling 8)
